wave: CORRECTNESS/SEMANTIC PRESERVATION -- close a documentation-vs-implementation mismatch in R4.10 CONCURRENCY's Spawn detection
wave_title: Pivoting to a genuinely fresh area per the prior generation's own note (R4.9 OWNERSHIP was checked first: its unemitted variants are explicitly labeled 'Reserved; never emitted this wave', a deliberate, already-made scope decision, not an oversight -- correctly left alone). R4.10 CONCURRENCY's own module doc comment, by contrast, explicitly frames the accepted spawn-detection risk as covering 'a function OR METHOD merely named spawn', but reading the actual code found only the free/path-call case (Expr::Call) was ever implemented -- a real gap between documented scope and actual behavior, not an intentional exclusion.
priority_classification: correctness (priority 1, since the doc comment already claimed a scope the code did not fulfill) / semantic preservation (priority 3, since this also expands real, useful coverage) -- a genuine documentation-vs-implementation mismatch is itself a correctness concern per this session's own 'do not leave docs claiming capabilities the code does not possess' principle.
how_the_gap_was_found: Read concurrency.rs's own module doc comment closely rather than only its code: 'a function or method merely named spawn (fn spawn() { .. }, game::spawn(enemy)) is not evidence of real concurrency' -- explicitly naming BOTH functions and methods as the accepted risk class. Then checked is_spawn_call's actual call sites and found it was only ever invoked from the Expr::Call arm; the Expr::MethodCall arm existed (to recurse into receiver/args) but never checked the method name at all. Confirmed via a failing test before writing the fix: pool.spawn(|| {}) produced zero Concurrency observations (left: 0, right: 1).
why_this_is_a_bug_not_a_deliberate_exclu: Unlike EFFECT's filesystem/process/network work (which deliberately excluded method calls because a BARE method name carries no qualifying module/type, making it far more ambiguous than a free/path call's own explicit qualifier), CONCURRENCY's spawn detection ALREADY accepts the identical bare-name ambiguity for the free-call case (its own doc comment cites `game::spawn(enemy)` as an accepted false-positive risk). There is no principled reason a bare `pool.spawn(..)` method call carries MORE risk than a bare `spawn(..)` free call already accepted -- excluding one while accepting the other was an implementation gap, not a considered boundary (confirmed by the doc comment's own pre-existing 'function OR method' framing predating this fix).

design_decisions.question: Reuse is_spawn_call (which calls call_callee_spelling, designed for free/path Expr::Call callees) for the method-call case too?
design_decisions.decision: No -- `method_call.method` is already a plain `syn::Ident`, so `method_call.method == "spawn"` is a direct, simpler check with no need to route through `call_callee_spelling` (which exists specifically to handle the more complex free/path-call callee-expression shape). Reusing the free-call helper would have added indirection without benefit.
